items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Narrator
Why does the medium popcorn cost almost as much as the large? It might be a decoy.
Narrator
Picture it: small, three dollars. Large, seven dollars. Now add a medium at six fifty.
Narrator
Suddenly the large looks like a steal. The medium isn't there to sell. It's there to make the large look cheap.
Narrator
The famous proof? An Economist offer: web, fifty-nine dollars. Print, a hundred and twenty-five. Print plus web, also a hundred and twenty-five.
Narrator
Dan Ariely said eighty-four percent of his students picked the combo. Remove the useless print option, and only thirty-two percent did.
Narrator
But here's the twist. That test used students, not real subscribers.
Narrator
Two of Ariely's other papers have since been retracted over data problems. And bigger studies found the decoy effect is often weak in real life.
Narrator
That's the mirage: even the trick about tricks can be an illusion.
Narrator
So don't fear the medium. Just ask: would I buy the large without it?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
